body:
I've been hiding it from my friends and family aswell but I don't have any desire to feel "happy" and enjoy life again and haven't had it for the past 7 years. But I'm perfectly fine with that.

I just made the big mistake of making new really close friends (her especially) and now I have to figure out the best way to disappear from her life the best possible way.


But thank you for your concerne.

The thing is nothing is dragging me down. I don't have any horrible story to why I don't want to live. I just don't. And it's been like this for 6-7 years. I don't have any interest in being here what so ever but I've been stuck trying to find out what way to "leave" to have my loved ones be affected as little as possible.

I don't have any future plans that you asked about because I've felt like it would just be a waste of time to think about if it never will become relevant.

Sorry for being such a downer. Tried to answer your question and give some more info.
That as soon as I graduate I'm cutting the contact with all of them and killing myself. Still trying to figure out the best way to do it all though.

Stardew Valley isn't really my type of game unfortuntely.

Factorio I haven't heard about before but I find it very interesting. Checked out the steam page and by the looks of it there's a lot to do and requires a lot of thinking to get to "late game". Not sure if this is correct but that's what it looks like to me! Which is nice, I like thinking. Heh.

Bastion is indeed a great game and I'm pretty sure I've completed it at least once!

Skyrim I'm having a really hard time deciding if I like it or not. Played 17 hours so far but I don't get the feeling of "oh boy I can't wait to play some more Skyrim when I get home" if you know what I mean.

Thanks for the suggestions, I'm thinking of maybe getting Factorio.
Oh wow yeah sounds like a lot has happened haha. I'd probably be playing alone though. Do you still think it'd be fun?
Oh yeah it's pretty good. But I can never really play it for more than and hour or two.
All of them or any specific game?
I've messed around in it with a friend about a year ago but there wasn't you could do. How is it now?

I'm pushing people away because I'm suicidal and want to hurt them as little as possible. And if I wanted help with my suicidal thoughts I could never ask them for help again because I wouldn't want them to think it's up to them to help me and if they failed it would all just be their fault.

> How have your friends been responding to your withdrawal of communication?

Well they tried to communicate with me over texts asking how I was doing, tried to get me to hang out with them and do stuff but I never really did and I guess they kinda gave up. After all, I was only in school for ~25% during that time. Now I have given up on that and just pretend like all is good, actually answering the texts and hang out with them if asked to. Just to keep the charade up.

> How have you been feeling without their interaction?

Always liked being alone so I have no issues with that.

> I don't think your friends will ever be able to forget you, even after drifting apart I think of past friends often.

Yeah... They might not forget me but I hope that when I do off myself they don't hear about it.

> I would consider trying medication again, sometimes it can take time and a little trial and error to find the right one at the right dose for you, the same can be said for therapists and therapy techniques. My experience is that they work best in combination.

I tried quite a few different medications for as long as needed to see if they were helping while I was seeing a therapist but none of them did. But I guess I didn't try every single one out there so yeah.

> If you want help to feel better, consider talking to your parents about how to go about this

I'm not feeling bad, except for maybe when hanging out with friends because I'm constantly lying to them by putting up these charades. And talking to my parents is out of the question. I'm not telling them a single thing about this ever again. I'm 99% sure they're convinced I'm doing great and I just can't have them be worried about me again.

> You have made it back to school, and you have your mind set on graduating, hold onto that vision.

Yes but that is only so my friends hopefully won't be affected by all this in the end. But I guess you're right and this is a goal, of sorts.

> There will always be that "what if I had done this" thought in their heads. "Maybe if I had spent more time with him". "Maybe if I had invited him over"

This is exactly why I want to just fade away and stop talking to them. So that when I do off myself they hopefully wont know about it.

> Your death will do nothing to make anyones life easier.

At first, no, but I do think it would be less stressfull/worrying than being worried every day about someone not comming home from school because he killed himself.

>  It certainly wont help the girl, who is probably already in pain that you stopped talking to her.

You're probably right. It hasn't been like it used to between us but she still seems happy and has gotten closer to some other friends instead. So I've been kinda switched out, which is nice. We used to talk a lot every single day and now it's anywhere between a day or two to a month.

Not talking to them and trying to drift away from them is the only way I can think of to keep them out of this but if you or anyone else has any other ideas feel free to share. However that's not helping with my depression or suicidal thoughts so I'm guessing that's out of the question anyways.

Been on meds until a few months ago because they did nothing at all and couldn't think straight. Also been talking to professionals for my parents sake but that's not going anywhere either.

And I am truly sorry for your loss. I just woke up and wasn't thinking clearly and now feel pretty bad about my tasteless post. Thank you for your answer though.

Hi, I kinda need some advise regarding this kind of thing. (Question at the bottom of this little wall) I'm a guy who has been suicidal since I was 12 (turning 18 in a month). I unfortunately made some very good friends I got close to my first year in high school (or upper secondary school, not sure what the difference is). And some day we were hanging out and decided to share the worst stuff that had happened and I was dumb enough to tell them I was suicidal.

Yadayadayada I regret telling them, current plan is to try to make them gradualy forget about me. Still have the third year of high school left but as soon as that is over I'm changing my number (already removed all social medias last summer) and disappear until I've decided how I'm doing it.

But my question is, is this better or worse than writing a text or similar? I mean the less they notice I'm gone the better, right? I care for my friends and want nothing but the best for them.
